expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "a confirm modal is rung-0 theater here" and "it protects nobody while adding friction to everyone"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "users... develop click-through blindness on 'Are you sure?' dialogs"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "Soft-delete + grace period (the real fix)... fully restorable for ~30 days, then hard-deleted by a job"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "Immediate undo toast. Delete fires right away... 'Workspace Deleted — Undo' for ~10s"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "use type-to-confirm (type the workspace name/slug) rather than a yes/no modal"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: Does not specify what retained dialogs should display about workspace or loss scale

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: States "This is a backend change, not a UI change" but does not explicitly note server-side enforcement requirement

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "strongest device first" with numbered list and "The confirm-modal instinct usually comes from treating the click as the failure point"
